keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 24-25; no Cliopatria row (its Xin shape ends in 23, ea-02-c). 'secured control of Yi Province and in 24 proclaimed himself king of Shu'; 'He controlled the entirety of the former Yi Province'. Sichuan and Chongqing stand for it; the page names no other province.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 26-36, CONFIDENCE 1 on Hanzhong: 'In 26 he sent Hou Dan to conquer the region of Hanzhong north of Sichuan'; the page does not say it was held, and gives only the Nan Commandery attack of 33 as failing ('did not advance far'). The rest is the 24-25 outline.

ledger.note: 24: Gongsun Shu proclaims himself King of Shu. He was 'the Administrator of Daojiang Commandery when the Xin regime fell in 23', 'secured control of Yi Province and in 24 proclaimed himself king of Shu'; in autumn 24 Gengshi's generals sent to take 'modern Sichuan, then held by the local warlord Gongsun Shu' were defeated (Gengshi page).

25: Gongsun Shu becomes Emperor of Chengjia. He 'asserted independence by adopting the title of Emperor of Cheng dynasty while adopting the era name of Longxing'; Chengdu is developed into an imperial capital. Same state, king to emperor.

region.text: the region of Hanzhong north of Sichuan

ledger.note: 26: Hanzhong attempted. 'In 26 he sent Hou Dan to conquer the region of Hanzhong north of Sichuan'; the opened pages do not say it was taken or who held it, so the gain is confidence 1 and the holder is entered as nobody.

region.text: Wei Ao's eastern Gansu, the Shuoning of the Guangwu page

ledger.note: 30: Wei Ao submits to Gongsun Shu. When Guangwu began a campaign against Wei in the summer of 30, Wei 'formally submitted to Gongsun and accepted a princely title, Prince of Shuoning, from him'. [Reviewer ea-02-x, 2026-10-19: the Guangwu page puts the submission in the passage on the summer-30 campaign but attaches no year to it; confidence lowered from 3 to 2]
34: Shuoning falls. 'In the winter of AD 34, Shuoning's capital Luomen fell, and Wei Chun surrendered' to the Eastern Han.

region.text: the entirety of the former Yi Province: 'modern Sichuan' (and Chongqing)

ledger.note: 35: Guangwu's army marches on Chengjia. 'In 35 Guangwu ordered an army to conquer Chengjia' and offered terms, 'which Gongsun refused'; the campaign 'lasted more than a year'. The Nan Commandery attack of 33 (Tian Rong and Yan Cen down the Three Gorges, 'did not advance far') took no ground and is not a contest.

region.text: the entirety of the former Yi Province: 'modern Sichuan' (and Chongqing)

ledger.note: 36: Chengdu falls. Wu Han and Zang Gong 'reached Chengdu with only a week's supplies left' in December 36; Gongsun was 'wounded in the battle' of 24 December and 'died in the night', and Chengdu's defenders under Yan Cen surrendered the following day.

ledger.note: 36: Yi Province passes to the Eastern Han. 'Gongsun was mortally wounded in battle, and Chengdu surrendered in the winter of AD 36'; the Guangwu footnote: he controlled all of China proper only on 25 December 36, when Chengdu surrendered.

region.text: the entirety of the former Yi Province: 'modern Sichuan' (and Chongqing)

ledger.note: 36: Chengjia ends with Gongsun Shu's death on 24 December 36; Wu Han ordered the massacre of his family and of Yan Cen and his family.

wars.name: Guangwu's conquest of Chengjia

zones.text: the entirety of the former Yi Province: 'modern Sichuan' (and Chongqing)

wars.outcome: The Eastern Han army took Chengdu on 24-25 December 36 after a campaign of more than a year; Gongsun Shu died of his wounds.
wars.note: The Guangwu page dates only the end. Earlier: Gengshi's generals defeated in Sichuan in autumn 24 (Gengshi page).

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for Chengjia beyond "the entirety of the former Yi Province".

notes:
Chengjia, Gongsun Shu's empire in Yi Province, 24-36. 3 pages opened (Gongsun Shu, Emperor Guangwu of Han, Gengshi Emperor); no Cliopatria row. The article title is 'Gongsun Shu'; the infobox state name is 'Chengjia'.
Unsettled: (1) whether Hou Dan's 26 attempt on Hanzhong succeeded (no page; confidence 1, holder entered as nobody); (2) the page gives Yi Province as 'modern Sichuan' (and Chongqing, parts of nearby provinces) without a boundary; (3) the Guangwu page puts the Eastern Han unification at 25 December 36 and the Gongsun Shu page the death at 24 December (month 12 on both); (4) Yunnan commanderies are not mentioned.
Counterparts: han-dynasty (ea-02-c has the 36 gain); xin-dynasty exists; liu-zhang (written by this batch) later held the same province.
